body:
Last night’s show featured a historic moment.
No, not the Virginia Supreme Court ruling.
Not the midterm redistricting chaos.
Not even the possibility that America someday elects President AOC (which, unfortunately, we had to discuss).
No.
The historic event was this:
I actually sold a prediction market position on time.
This basically never happens.
Normally, I ride these things all the way to the bitter end, chasing the last few cents like a degenerate raccoon digging through a back alley dumpster.
But this time, I behaved like a functional adult.
Back during Super Bowl weekend, while millions of people were watching football and living healthy social lives, I was buying shares in Virginia redistricting markets.
Which is super cool, I know.
The basic thesis was simple:
Virginia’s legislature tried to rush through redistricting changes in a way that looked legally questionable from the start. The timeline didn’t make sense. The process didn’t make sense. And once you looked carefully at how early voting complicated the constitutional requirements, the entire thing started looking shaky.
The market didn’t seem to fully price that in.
So I bought the “No” side at 44 cents.
Then the Virginia Supreme Court came in and essentially said: yeah, you can’t do this.
The market exploded upward.
And though many times in this spot I try and ride things out too long… I actually sold at 94 cents instead of waiting for the final six.
Which turned out to be the correct move because the market immediately started drifting backward again afterward.
Yay me!
But the really important part isn’t my temporary emotional maturity.
It’s what this ruling means for the broader midterm picture.
Because redistricting has quietly become one of the biggest forces shaping the 2026 House markets.
And over the past couple weeks, those markets have moved HARD.
A lot of people still think Democrats are cruising toward taking the House because that’s historically what happens during midterms.
And honestly? Structurally, Republicans are still facing a difficult environment.
Gas prices are high.

War headlines are everywhere.

Trump fatigue absolutely exists outside conservative media bubbles.

And midterms historically punish the party in power.
All true.
But what changed is the map.
Last night, we walked through the district-by-district shifts happening across states like Virginia, Tennessee, and Florida, and some of these flips are enormous.
Districts that looked safely Democratic suddenly became toss-ups.

Republican odds in several markets swung violently upward almost overnight.

And the overall House probability has started inching back toward the GOP after Democrats previously looked almost untouchable.
Not favored.
But competitive.
That’s a big difference.
One of the most important lessons in prediction markets is understanding when a market moves from “wrong” to merely “less wrong.”
Because value doesn’t appear when you perfectly predict the future.
Value appears when the market overreacts.
That’s where things may be heading again with the House markets.
We also spent a big chunk of the show doing something far more important than redistricting:
A fantasy-style 2028 presidential draft.
It’s VERY early, obviously, and staring at 2028 prediction markets for too long comes with its own risk. Your brain starts breaking in real time trying to think about all the possibilities.
At one point, we were seriously debating the upside potential of Donald Trump Jr.
At another point, my guest Dan Andros and I ended up on opposite sides of an AOC market. 
We also broke down why JD Vance may still be undervalued, why Marco Rubio’s surge is more complicated than it looks, and why Josh Shapiro keeps hovering around the edge of the Democratic conversation.
But maybe the most important part of that segment had nothing to do with the candidates themselves.
It was about time.
One of the biggest mistakes people make in prediction markets is ignoring the clock.
A position that looks attractive at first glance suddenly looks a lot less attractive when you realize your money could be tied up for three years just to earn a relatively small percentage return.
That’s where people get trapped.
Not because their political analysis was wrong.
Because their market analysis was incomplete.
There’s a difference.
And honestly, I think a lot of people miss it.
Anyway, there was a lot packed into this one:
Virginia redistricting.

Midterm map changes.

House market movement.

Prediction market strategy.

2028 fantasy drafting.

And one long-shot presidential position that sounds ridiculous now… but maybe not forever.
That part starts about halfway through the episode.
